He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. ==High school career== Tilmon played basketball for [[East St. Louis Senior High School]] in [[East St. Louis, Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Alec |title=Meet MU's Tilmon, the man born for Braggin' Rights |url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/meet-mus-tilmon-the-man-born-for-braggin-rights/article_95c5f4ea-e10e-11e7-8a05-ff9d227d1afb.html |website=[[Columbia Missourian]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=December 17, 2017}} He transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]] for his junior season, averaging 13.2 points and 8.2 rebounds per game for one of the best teams in the country. He dislocated his left shoulder at the High School Nationals title game and underwent surgery. He returned to East St. Louis for his senior season.{{cite web |title=Illinois commit Jeremiah Tilmon transfers back to East St. Louis |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/preps-talk/illinois-commit-jeremiah-tilmon-transfers-back-east-st-louis |website=NBC Sports |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=August 16, 2016}} He averaged 15.3 points, 11 rebounds and four blocks per game and was a First Team All-State selection.{{cite web |last1=Melroe |first1=Andrew |title="The Perfect Storm" - Jeremiah Tilmon Ready To Make Impact |url=https://mutigers.com/news/2017/8/14/mens-basketball-the-perfect-storm-jeremiah-tilmon-ready-to-make-impact.aspx |website=University of Missouri Athletics |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=August 14, 2017}} He originally committed to playing college basketball for [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] but reopened his recruitment after coach [[John Groce]] was fired. Tilmon later committed to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], choosing the Tigers over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Former Illinois commit Jeremiah Tilmon signs with Missouri |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-jeremiah-tilmon-signs-with-missouri-20170515-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=May 15, 2017}} ==College career== Before his freshman season at Missouri, Tilmon was arrested for a [[Minor in Possession]].{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Daniel |title=Jeremiah Tilmon arrested for minor in possession |url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/sports/20170619/jeremiah-tilmon-arrested-for-minor-in-possession |website=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=June 19, 2017 |archive-date=February 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205092112/https://www.columbiatribune.com/sports/20170619/jeremiah-tilmon-arrested-for-minor-in-possession |url-status=dead }} As a freshman, he averaged 8.2 points and 4.2 rebounds per game in a starting role.{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |title=Learn from regret: Missouri's Jeremiah Tilmon went to work to overhaul his game, strengthen his mind |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/552288/2018/10/02/learn-from-regret-missouris-jeremiah-tilmon-went-to-work-to-overhaul-his-game-strengthen-his-mind/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=October 2, 2018}} On December 18, 2018, Tilmon recorded a sophomore season-high 23 points and 10 rebounds in a 71–56 win over [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |title=Eye of the Tiger: Jeremiah Tilmon finally coming into his own as he powers Mizzou to victory over Xavier |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/722976/2018/12/19/eye-of-the-tiger-jeremiah-tilmon-finally-coming-into-his-own-as-he-powers-mizzou-to-victory-over-xavier/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=December 18, 2018}} As a sophomore, he averaged 10.1 points and 5.9 rebounds per game. Tilmon declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] before withdrawing his name and returning to college.{{cite web |last1=DeArmond |first1=Gabe |last2=Forde |first2=Mitchell |title=Tilmon to test draft waters |url=https://missouri.rivals.com/news/tilmon-to-test-draft-waters |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=April 15, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 8.2 points and 4.4 rebounds per game and was limited to 17 games due to a foot injury. Tilmon declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but returned to Missouri for his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Blum |first1=Eric |title=Mizzou's Tilmon: 'I plan on returning, finishing strong' |url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/story/sports/2020/07/06/mizzoursquos-tilmon-i-plan-on-returning-finishing-strong/42495921/ |website=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=July 6, 2020}} On January 30, 2021, he posted 33 points and 11 rebounds in a 102–98 overtime victory over [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].{{cite web |last1=Ladd |first1=Aaron |title=Tigers top TCU in OT; Tilmon, Pinson set career-highs |url=https://www.kshb.com/sports/tigers-top-tcu-in-ot-tilmon-pinson-set-career-highs |website=[[KSHB-TV]] |access-date=January 31, 2021 |date=January 30, 2021}} As a senior, Tilmon averaged 12.4 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game. He was named to the Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]].{{cite news |last1=Blum |first1=Eric |title=Mizzou alumni Jeremiah Tilmon, Dru Smith get NBA chances with Magic, Heat |url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/story/sports/nba/2021/07/30/nba-draft-2021-mizzou-alumni-jeremiah-tilmon-dru-smith-get-nba-chances-florida-squads/5431834001/ |access-date=September 2, 2021 |work=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]] |date=July 30, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Lakeland Magic (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Tilmon joined the [[Orlando Magic]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|first=Anthony|last=Kristensen|title=Smith, Tilmon playing in NBA Summer League|url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/smith-tilmon-playing-in-nba-summer-league/article_a8d529e0-fafd-11eb-bc37-1ba26373d151.html|work=[[Columbia Missourian]]|date=August 11, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}} On October 7, 2021, Tilmon signed with the Magic,{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Jeremiah Tilmon|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jeremiah-tilmon-20211007|website=NBA.com|date=October 7, 2021|access-date=October 8, 2021}} but was waived five days later.{{cite tweet|author=Orlando Magic PR|number=1448022660420620290|title=PRESS RELEASE: @OrlandoMagic sign free agent @devin_cannady3; Waive Jeremiah Tilmon #MagicTogether|user=Magic_PR|date=October 12, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 28, he joined the [[Lakeland Magic]] as an affiliate player{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}} and in 45 games, he averaged 9.7 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 20.5 minutes.{{cite web|title=Honey Badgers Sign NBA G League Forward Tilmon|url=https://www.cebl.ca/honey-badgers-sign-nba-g-league-forward-tilmon|website=CEBL.com|date=May 3, 2022|access-date=May 3, 2022}} ===Hamilton Honey Badgers (2022)=== On May 3, 2022, Tilmon signed with the [[Brampton Honey Badgers|Hamilton Honey Badgers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League|CEBL]]. On August 14, he won the franchise's first CEBL championship with the Honey Badgers.{{Cite web |date=August 15, 2022 |title=Agada And Vital Carry Honey Badgers To First Championship In Club History |url=https://www.cebl.ca/agada-and-vital-carry-honey-badgers-to-first-championship-in-club-history |access-date=August 15, 2022 |website=www.cebl.ca |language=en}} ===Raptors 905 (2022–2023)=== On December 28, 2022, Tilmon was traded to the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=December 28, 2022|access-date=December 28, 2022}} On January 25, 2023, Tilmon was acquired as a returning player.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=January 25, 2023}} ===Brampton Honey Badgers (2023)=== On April 13, 2023, Tilmon signed with the [[Brampton Honey Badgers]].{{cite web|title=Honey Badgers Re-Sign Tilmon Jr. for Second Season|url=https://www.cebl.ca/honey-badgers-re-sign-tilmon-jr-for-second-season|website=CEBL.com|date=April 13, 2022|access-date=April 13, 2022}} On June 23, 2023, Tilmon signed with the [[Kagoshima Rebnise]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite web|title=【新規】Jeremiah Tilmon選手 2023-24シーズン 選手契約締結のお知らせ|url=https://www.rebnise.jp/news/detail/id=15221|website=Rebnise.jp|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=August 2, 2023|language=Japanese}} On September 29, his contract was terminated.{{cite web |title=ジェレマイア・ティルモン選手 契約解除のお知らせ |url=https://www.rebnise.jp/news/detail/id=15406 |publisher=鹿児島レブナイズ |access-date=August 16, 2024 |date=September 29, 2023}} ===Greensboro Swarm (2023–2024)=== On October 29, 2023, Tilmon signed with the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster and Coaching Staff for 2023-24 Season|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-announce-training-camp-roster-and-coaching-staff-for-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2023}} ===Al Qadsia (2024)=== On April 1, 2024, Tilmon signed with the [[Qadsia SC|Al Qadsia]] of the [[Kuwaiti Division I Basketball League]].{{cite web|first=Ahmad|last=Madwar|title=Qadsia lands Jeremiah Tilmon Jr.|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Kuwait/news/863141/Qadsia-lands-Jeremiah-Tilmon-Jr.|website=Asia-Basket.com|date=April 1, 2024|access-date=April 2, 2024}} ===Metros de Santiago (2024)=== On June 19, 2024, Tilmon signed with the [[Metros de Santiago]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].{{cite web |title=LNB 2024 - Metros land Jeremiah Tilmon Jr., ex Qadsia |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Dominican-Republic/news/877064/LNB-2024---Metros-land-Jeremiah-Tilmon-Jr.,-ex-Qadsia |publisher=Eurobasket.com |access-date=August 16, 2024 |date=June 19, 2024}} ===Suwon KT Sonicboom (2024)=== On June 28, 2024, Tilmon signed with the [[Suwon KT Sonicboom]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].{{cite web |title='외국선수 구성 완료' KT, G리그 출신 빅맨 틸먼과 계약 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065585199130609 |publisher=점프볼 |access-date=August 16, 2024 |date=June 28, 2024}} On November 18, he was replaced by [[Jordan Morgan (basketball)|Jordan Morgan]].{{cite web |title=KT, 외국 선수 교체 단행... 틸먼 대신 204cm 장신 센터 조던 모건 영입 |url=https://www.rookie.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=103106 |publisher=ROOKIE |access-date=December 4, 2024 |date=November 18, 2024}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2025–2026)=== On November 7, 2025, Tilmon was named to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2025-26-opening-night-roster|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2025-26 OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 7, 2025|access-date=November 7, 2025}} === Winnipeg Sea Bears (2026–present) === On April 22, 2026, Tilmon signed with the [[Winnipeg Sea Bears]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL).
